File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("26351aed0397158d3a3b8cc8fd3047d4c015d264c9895f10f20f1521b974ed18", "36ff00b45e67baa7e3674b0c80f48e88737264c61e5c6b3b091200972de8157c") or SHA1 in~ ("26351aed0397158d3a3b8cc8fd3047d4c015d264c9895f10f20f1521b974ed18", "36ff00b45e67baa7e3674b0c80f48e88737264c61e5c6b3b091200972de8157c") or MD5 in~ ("26351aed0397158d3a3b8cc8fd3047d4c015d264c9895f10f20f1521b974ed18", "36ff00b45e67baa7e3674b0c80f48e88737264c61e5c6b3b091200972de8157c")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("26351aed0397158d3a3b8cc8fd3047d4c015d264c9895f10f20f1521b974ed18", "36ff00b45e67baa7e3674b0c80f48e88737264c61e5c6b3b091200972de8157c") or SHA1 in~ ("26351aed0397158d3a3b8cc8fd3047d4c015d264c9895f10f20f1521b974ed18", "36ff00b45e67baa7e3674b0c80f48e88737264c61e5c6b3b091200972de8157c") or MD5 in~ ("26351aed0397158d3a3b8cc8fd3047d4c015d264c9895f10f20f1521b974ed18", "36ff00b45e67baa7e3674b0c80f48e88737264c61e5c6b3b091200972de8157c")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["26351aed0397158d3a3b8cc8fd3047d4c015d264c9895f10f20f1521b974ed18", "36ff00b45e67baa7e3674b0c80f48e88737264c61e5c6b3b091200972de8157c"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

// Article-specific bespoke detection — Two Compromised joyfill npm Packages Run RAT When Imported Into Node.js

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High

ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48027", "CVE-2026-45321")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48027", "CVE-2026-45321")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79") or SHA1 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79") or MD5 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79") or SHA1 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79") or MD5 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable @hypequery/clickhouse dependency present (< 2.0.2, CVE-2026-54658) AIExploitation High
Inventories hosts/containers where the @hypequery/clickhouse npm package is installed (node_modules/@hypequery/clickhouse) or flagged by TVM for CVE-2026-54658. This is the first-line exposure hunt for the SQL-injection-in-escapeValue advisory before any exploitation is attempted. Rationale: Uses the exact vulnerable package coordinate (@hypequery/clickhouse) and node_modules path plus the assigned CVE-2026-54658; a package-present hunt is the highest-confidence exposure signal for a dependency advisory with no IOCs. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6wcc-39rp-hh9p • https://cve.threatint.com/CVE/CVE-2026-54658 • https://advisories.gitlab.com/advisories/
ATT&CKT1190 T1195.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Dev/CI build agents that legitimately install the package as part of the app
  • Hosts already upgraded to 2.0.2+ (file-presence check can't read the installed version)
  • npm/yarn offline mirror or cache directories holding the tarball
  • Monorepos with multiple hoisted copies of the package inflating FileCount
  • Container base-image scanning sandboxes that pull all dependency versions
Suppression filter
| where SoftwareVersion !startswith "2.0.2" and toint(split(SoftwareVersion, ".")[0]) < 2
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): For each host, confirm the installed version — read package.json/package-lock.json under @hypequery/clickhouse and check whether it is < 2.0.2; cross-reference the TVM CveId hit. Step 2 (contain): For confirmed <2.0.2 on internet-facing/user-facing services, prioritise `npm install @hypequery/clickhouse@2.0.2` (or later) and redeploy; there is no runtime workaround per the advisory. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot to UC-2/UC-3 web and DB query-log detections for that host to determine whether the injection was already attempted before patching.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has_any (@"@hypequery\clickhouse", "@hypequery/clickhouse")
| summarize FileCount = count(), FoldersSeen = make_set(FolderPath, 25), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, DeviceId
| order by LastSeen desc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

| where CveId == "CVE-2026-54658"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, DeviceId, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by TimeGenerated desc

@hypequery/clickhouse SQLi: backslash-quote escape bypass in web/API request parameters AIExploitation Medium
Hunts inbound HTTP/WAF request parameters that carry the CVE-2026-54658 exploitation primitive — a value with a trailing backslash immediately preceding a single quote (raw \' or URL-encoded %5C%27) — combined with SQL follow-on keywords. This is the on-the-wire signature of an attacker escaping the closing quote emitted by escapeValue(). Rationale: Encodes the article's precise exploitation mechanic — 'trailing backslash to escape the closing quote' — as a backslash-quote (\' / %5C%27) token gated by SQL keywords, so it fires on the injection attempt rather than a generic SQLi template. Requires the app to sit behind a WAF/reverse-proxy that logs request payloads; Defender has no web-log table (left empty). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6wcc-39rp-hh9p • https://cve.threatint.com/CVE/CVE-2026-54658
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security scanners (Burp/ZAP/Nuclei/Acunetix) running authorised SQLi test payloads
  • Legitimate query strings containing Windows paths ending in a backslash before a quoted value
  • Analytics dashboards passing ClickHouse system.* table names in URL filters
  • Encoded file paths in file-manager apps producing %5C sequences
  • Pen-test engagements from known internal source IPs
Suppression filter
| where DestinationHostName !has_any ("scanner", "appsec", "pentest") and SourceIP !in ("10.10.10.0")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Decode the RequestURL/Payload and confirm the backslash precedes the string-terminating quote (not a legitimate escaped path); note SourceIP, destination host and whether the target app depends on @hypequery/clickhouse (UC-1). Step 2 (contain): Block the SourceIP at the WAF and, if the target is <2.0.2, take the endpoint out of rotation / apply the 2.0.2 upgrade. Step 3 (hunt): Correlate the same SourceIP across other parameters/endpoints and pivot to UC-3/UC-4 on the backend DB host to confirm whether the injected SQL actually executed.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| extend Payload = strcat(tostring(RequestURL), " ", tostring(RequestContext), " ", tostring(Message))
| where Payload matches regex @"(?i)(\\'|%5c%27)"
| where Payload has_any ("UNION", "SELECT", "OR 1=1", "OR%201=1", " OR ", "--", "/*", "system.", "FROM system")
| where isempty(SourceUserName) or SourceUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestMethod, RequestURL, Payload
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: SQL injection backslash-quote escape in web request (CVE-2026-54658 primitive)
id: 7b2c8f14-3d6a-4e29-9f5b-8a1c0e7d6b52
description: Detects the trailing-backslash-then-quote escape primitive (raw or URL-encoded) with SQL follow-on keywords in HTTP request parameters, matching @hypequery/clickhouse escapeValue() bypass.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6wcc-39rp-hh9p
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/29
tags:
  - attack.t1190
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  escape:
    c-uri-query|contains:
      - "\\'"
      - '%5C%27'
      - '%5c%27'
  sqlkw:
    c-uri-query|contains:
      - 'UNION'
      - 'SELECT'
      - 'OR 1=1'
      - 'OR%201=1'
      - '--'
      - 'system.'
  condition: escape and sqlkw
level: high
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*%5C%27*" OR Web.url="*%5c%27*" OR Web.url="*\\'*") AND (Web.url="*UNION*" OR Web.url="*SELECT*" OR Web.url="*OR%201=1*" OR Web.url="*--*" OR Web.url="*system.*") by Web.src Web.dest Web.http_method Web.url Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)` | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*%5C%27*" OR Web.url="*%5c%27*" OR Web.url="*\\'*") AND (Web.url="*UNION*" OR Web.url="*SELECT*" OR Web.url="*OR%201=1*" OR Web.url="*--*" OR Web.url="*system.*") by Web.src Web.dest Web.http_method Web.url Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)` | sort - lastTime
ClickHouse query_log shows injected SQL from @hypequery escapeValue bypass AIExploitation Medium
Hunts ClickHouse server/query logs (shipped via Syslog) for statements containing the backslash-quote escape artifact together with injection follow-on SQL (UNION, OR 1=1, access to system.* tables). This is where CVE-2026-54658 exploitation becomes visible as actually-executed arbitrary SQL on the database tier. Rationale: Targets the backend evidence of 'arbitrary SQL execution' by matching the same backslash-quote artifact plus injection keywords in ClickHouse query logs; higher fidelity than the web-edge UC because it confirms the statement reached and parsed on the DB. Depends on ClickHouse logs being forwarded to Syslog/Datadog (noted); no Defender equivalent. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6wcc-39rp-hh9p • https://cve.threatint.com/CVE/CVE-2026-54658
ATT&CKT1190
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate application queries that read from ClickHouse system.* tables (dashboards, monitoring)
  • Data-migration or admin scripts using UNION for legitimate merges
  • String literals in analytics data that naturally contain \' sequences
  • Query replay from load-testing tools
  • Backup/ETL jobs enumerating system.parts or system.tables
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the full matching query and its originating user/client from query_log; determine whether the backslash-quote breaks out of a parameter string vs. appearing inside a legitimate literal. Step 2 (contain): If injection is confirmed, revoke the DB user/API credential the app uses, isolate the app host, and force the 2.0.2 upgrade. Step 3 (hunt): Enumerate all queries from the same client_id/initial_user around the event for data-exfiltration (SELECT from sensitive tables), and correlate back to the UC-2 web request that delivered the payload.
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where ProcessName has "clickhouse" or SyslogMessage has "clickhouse"
| where SyslogMessage matches regex @"(?i)(\\'|%5c%27)"
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("UNION", "OR 1=1", " OR ", "system.", "FROM system", "--", "/*")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:linux.syslog @process.name:clickhouse-server (*\\'* OR *%5c%27*) AND (*UNION* OR *"OR 1=1"* OR *system.* OR *"FROM system"*)
APPLICATION
index=* (sourcetype=clickhouse OR sourcetype=clickhouse:query_log OR source="*clickhouse-server*")
| regex _raw="(?i)(\\'|%5c%27)"
| search ("UNION" OR "OR 1=1" OR " OR 1=1" OR "system." OR "FROM system" OR "--")
| stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(host) as hosts by _raw
| sort - count
ClickHouse SQL syntax-error spike from @hypequery/clickhouse injection probing AIExploitation Low
Threshold hunt for a burst of ClickHouse SYNTAX_ERROR (Code: 62) / escapeValue-related exceptions on an application host, indicating an attacker iterating backslash-quote payloads against CVE-2026-54658 before a working injection lands. Failed injection attempts leave parser errors even when the successful one does not. Rationale: Names the article's escapeValue() function and the vulnerable package, plus ClickHouse's SYNTAX_ERROR code (62) that malformed injection payloads trigger; an error-rate spike is a cheap early-warning for injection fuzzing that the pattern-match UCs may miss when payloads are encoded. Telemetry depends on app/DB error logs reaching Syslog/Datadog. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6wcc-39rp-hh9p • https://cve.threatint.com/CVE/CVE-2026-54658
ATT&CKT1190
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Buggy application release emitting genuine malformed queries after a deploy
  • Developer/analyst ad-hoc query session with typos against the same ClickHouse
  • Schema-migration window where queries reference not-yet-created columns
  • BI tool generating invalid SQL for unsupported functions
  • Load/chaos testing that intentionally sends malformed statements
Suppression filter
| where Sample !has_any ("migration", "ALTER TABLE", "CREATE TABLE")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Inspect the sample error messages and the client/user generating them — a single external client driving the spike with backslash-quote payloads is malicious; a recent app deploy is likely benign. Step 2 (contain): If external and injection-shaped, block the source at the WAF, revoke the app's DB credential, and schedule the 2.0.2 upgrade. Step 3 (hunt): Look for one successful (non-error) query from the same client immediately after the error burst (the payload that worked) and pivot to UC-3 to assess data access.
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where (SyslogMessage has "Code: 62" and SyslogMessage has "Syntax error") or SyslogMessage has "escapeValue" or SyslogMessage has "@hypequery/clickhouse"
| summarize ErrCount = count(), Sample = any(SyslogMessage), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by Computer, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where ErrCount > 20   // 20 = burst threshold: normal apps emit near-zero ClickHouse syntax errors per 5m
| order by LastSeen desc
source:linux.syslog @process.name:clickhouse-server ((*"Code: 62"* AND *"Syntax error"*) OR *escapeValue* OR *@hypequery/clickhouse*)
APPLICATION
index=* (sourcetype=clickhouse OR sourcetype=clickhouse:query_log OR source="*clickhouse-server*")
| search ("Code: 62" "Syntax error") OR "escapeValue" OR "@hypequery/clickhouse"
| bin _time span=5m
| stats count as errCount values(host) as hosts by _time
| where errCount > 20
| sort - _time
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-54658")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-54658")

goshs WebDAV --no-delete bypass: blocked DELETE followed by successful MOVE on same path AIExploitation High
Hunts the CVE-2026-64863 exploit signature where an attacker probes the --no-delete restriction (DELETE returns 403) and then destroys the same resource via the WebDAV MOVE verb (201 Created / 204 No Content). The 403-then-2xx pairing on an identical URL within a short window is the bypass fingerprint, not generic WebDAV usage. Rationale: Uses the article's exact control-vs-bypass pairing: DELETE=403 (blocked by --no-delete) then MOVE=201/204 (RemoveAll/rename succeeds). Correlating both on the same URL from the same source removes benign WebDAV MOVE traffic, which never co-occurs with a just-refused DELETE on the identical path. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/goshs.de/goshs/v2/CVE-2026-64863/ • https://cve.threatint.com/CVE/CVE-2026-64863
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A WebDAV sync client (Finder/Explorer) that retries a delete as a rename after a transient 403 for reasons unrelated to policy
  • Automated backup tooling that first attempts DELETE, is denied, and falls back to MOVE-to-archive on the same object
  • Load/security scanners (e.g. Nessus WebDAV checks) exercising both verbs against the same test path
  • Reverse proxy that rewrites and duplicates request lines, double-logging one client action as two verbs
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the target server is goshs (<= v2.1.3) — check the response Server header 'goshs/...' and whether it was launched with '-w --no-delete'; pull the full request sequence for the src IP against the affected URL. 2) Contain: block the src IP at the WAF/proxy and stop/upgrade the goshs instance to v2.1.4 (or drop WebDAV write verbs MOVE/COPY at the proxy) so the --no-delete boundary is actually enforced. 3) Hunt: enumerate every MOVE 201/204 from that src across all served paths to scope which artefacts were renamed away or overwritten, and check file integrity of the served directory against a known-good manifest.
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where csMethod in ("DELETE","MOVE")
| extend DeleteBlocked = iff(csMethod == "DELETE" and scStatus == 403, 1, 0)
| extend MoveSuccess = iff(csMethod == "MOVE" and scStatus in (201, 204), 1, 0)
| where DeleteBlocked == 1 or MoveSuccess == 1
| summarize DeleteBlocked = sum(DeleteBlocked), MoveSuccess = sum(MoveSuccess), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Statuses = make_set(scStatus) by cIP, csUriStem, Computer, sSiteName
| where DeleteBlocked > 0 and MoveSuccess > 0
| order by LastSeen desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Web where (Web.http_method="DELETE" AND Web.status=403) OR (Web.http_method="MOVE" AND Web.status IN (201,204)) by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.dest_port, Web.url, Web.http_method, Web.status, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| eval delete_blocked=if(http_method=="DELETE" AND status=="403",1,0)
| eval move_success=if(http_method=="MOVE" AND (status=="201" OR status=="204"),1,0)
| stats sum(delete_blocked) as delete_blocked, sum(move_success) as move_success, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime, values(status) as statuses by src, dest, dest_port, url
| where delete_blocked>0 AND move_success>0
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web where (Web.http_method="DELETE" AND Web.status=403) OR (Web.http_method="MOVE" AND Web.status IN (201,204)) by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.dest_port, Web.url, Web.http_method, Web.status, _time span=1m

| stats sum(delete_blocked) as delete_blocked, sum(move_success) as move_success, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime, values(status) as statuses by src, dest, dest_port, url
| where delete_blocked>0 AND move_success>0
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
WebDAV MOVE/COPY write-verb succeeds against goshs artifact server (Overwrite:T destination clobber) AIExploitation Medium
Surfaces successful WebDAV MOVE/COPY verbs (201/204) against an exposed goshs file server, the mechanism CVE-2026-64863 abuses to rename-away or, with the 'Overwrite: T' header, RemoveAll and overwrite existing files under --no-delete. MOVE/COPY are rare in normal artifact-download traffic, so a success is a high-signal exploitation candidate. Rationale: Keys on the article's exploitation primitive — the WebDAV MOVE/COPY verbs returning 201/204 — plus the 'Overwrite: T' header called out as the RemoveAll trigger (grep RequestContext/Message where the WAF logs headers). MOVE/COPY are near-absent in legitimate file-download workloads, so a success against a goshs host is worth a hunt even without correlation. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/patrickhener/goshs/CVE-2026-64863/ • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/goshs.de/goshs/v2/CVE-2026-50138/
ATT&CKT1190 T1485
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate WebDAV clients (Finder, Windows Explorer, Cyberduck) renaming files on a genuinely writable goshs share (no --no-delete set)
  • CI/CD or backup jobs that use MOVE to atomically publish artifacts into the served directory
  • SharePoint/Nextcloud or other WebDAV appliances behind the same WAF that legitimately use MOVE/COPY
  • Web content-management operations issuing COPY for versioning
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the destination is a goshs instance and whether it runs with --no-delete/--read-only; inspect the request for a 'Destination:' and 'Overwrite: T' header (header-logging WAFs) that indicates intent to clobber an existing file. 2) Contain: strip MOVE/COPY at the proxy for that vhost and upgrade goshs to v2.1.4; restrict the WebDAV port to trusted source ranges. 3) Hunt: pivot on the src IP to list all MOVE/COPY targets and any preceding blocked DELETE (see companion rule) to determine which served files were destroyed or overwritten.

| where RequestMethod in ("MOVE", "COPY")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestMethod, RequestURL, RequestContext, DeviceProduct, DeviceVendor, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc

goshs process deletes or renames served files while launched with --no-delete (impact confirmation) AIActions on Objectives High
Confirms real data loss from CVE-2026-64863 on the host: a goshs process removing or renaming files (os.Rename / RemoveAll) even though it was started with --no-delete. Under that flag goshs should never delete anything, so any goshs-initiated file delete/rename event is a direct policy violation and proof the WebDAV MOVE bypass fired. Rationale: Combines the article's process (goshs) with its stated invariant (--no-delete means no deletion) — so a goshs-initiated FileDeleted/FileRenamed with '--no-delete' on the command line is a definitional bypass with essentially no benign explanation. This is the on-host impact confirmation for the HTTP-layer rules. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/goshs.de/goshs/v2/CVE-2026-64863/ • https://github.com/goshs-labs/goshs/releases
ATT&CKT1485 T1070.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • goshs writing/cleaning up transient files for the ?bulk zip-download feature (temporary archive creation, not served-file deletion)
  • An operator manually deleting files in the served directory with another tool (would not show goshs as the initiating process)
  • goshs launched without --no-delete performing intended deletes (excluded by the --no-delete command-line filter)
  • Log-rotation or the goshs binary being self-updated/replaced on disk (rename of the binary rather than served content)
Suppression filter
// Defender: exclude self-update/binary replacement and keep only served-content paths
| where not (FileName endswith "goshs" or FileName endswith "goshs.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the InitiatingProcessCommandLine to confirm --no-delete/--webdav were set, and capture FolderPath/PreviousFolderPath to identify exactly which served file was renamed or removed. 2) Contain: stop the goshs service and upgrade to v2.1.4 (or remove WebDAV); restore the affected file(s) from backup, as MOVE/RemoveAll destroys the original content. 3) Hunt: correlate the file event timestamp back to the WebDAV access log for the matching MOVE 201/204 and its source IP to attribute the actor, and review whether other files in the same directory disappeared in the same window.
DeviceFileEvents

| where InitiatingProcessFileName startswith "goshs"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "--no-delete"
| where ActionType in ("FileDeleted", "FileRenamed")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, PreviousFolderPath, PreviousFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent

| where ActingProcessName has "goshs"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "--no-delete"
| where EventType in ("FileDeleted", "FileRenamed")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable goshs SFTP launch: empty-credential basic-auth (-b 'user:' / ':pass') with -sftp and no -fkf AIExploitation High
Hunts the exact vulnerable configuration for CVE-2026-62325 / CVE-2026-40884: a goshs process started with -sftp and a -b basic-auth string that has an empty username or empty password, and without -fkf (public-key). This combination disables the SFTP PasswordHandler (gliderlabs/ssh sets NoClientAuth=true), exposing unauthenticated file read/write/delete/rename. Article-specific because it keys on the literal goshs binary and its -b/-sftp/-fkf flag semantics, not a generic SSH check. Rationale: Uses the article's literal vulnerable invocation `goshs -b 'admin:' -sftp` and the flag logic (`-b` empty-side + `-sftp` + absence of `-fkf`) that produces NoClientAuth=true. The empty-credential regex catches both the CVE-2026-62325 empty-password variant and the CVE-2026-40884 empty-username variant. Cross-checked against the SentinelOne CVE-2026-40884 entry and the GHSA-c29w-qq4m-2gcv GitLab advisory. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sentinelone.com/vulnerability-database/cve-2026-40884/ • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/patrickhener/goshs/GHSA-c29w-qq4m-2gcv/ • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rjrw-mjq6-hpmm
ATT&CKT1190 T1021.004 T1133
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Pentester/red-team intentionally running goshs as a throwaway file server on an engagement host
  • CTF or lab boxes where goshs is deliberately started with weak auth for training
  • Automation/scripts that pass -b with a trailing colon by mistake but on an internal-only isolated host
  • Security researcher reproducing the CVE in a sandbox
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("pentest", "redteam", "ctf", "lab") and InitiatingProcessAccountName has_any ("pentest", "redteam"))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Confirm the exact `-b` value and whether `-fkf` is absent; identify the listening port and whether the host is internet-facing (check DeviceInfo.IsInternetFacing / firewall NAT). 2) CONTAIN: Kill the goshs process and block the SFTP listener port at the host firewall; if internet-facing, treat as actively exploitable and isolate the host. 3) HUNT: Pivot to UC2/UC3 — enumerate inbound SFTP connections this goshs PID accepted and every file it read/wrote/deleted; determine data exposure and whether any remote client IP is external.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName has "goshs" or ProcessCommandLine has "goshs"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "-sftp"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "-b"
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "-fkf"
// empty-password ( user: ) or empty-username ( :pass ) in the -b basic-auth string
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)-b\s+['""]?([^\s'"":]+:(?:['""]|\s|$)|:[^\s'""]+)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate

| order by TimeGenerated desc

Endpoint traffic to cubepilot.org during 24 Jul 2026 DNS-hijack / AiTM window AIDelivery Medium
Retro-hunt for any host that resolved or connected to cubepilot.org or its subdomains (portal, discuss/forum, docs) during the 24 July 2026 DNS-hijack window, when traffic was redirected to attacker infrastructure holding fraudulent TLS certs. Any credentials entered on those services may have been captured. Surfaces the resolved RemoteIP so an analyst can identify the attacker-controlled address. Rationale: Anchors on the exact victim domain (cubepilot.org and subdomains portal/discuss/docs confirmed on CubePilot's own security notice) bounded to the 24 Jul 2026 hijack window; make_set on RemoteIP/DnsResponseName surfaces the attacker-controlled resolution so no attacker IP needs to be hardcoded. Cross-checked against: • https://cubepilot.com/security-notice/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cubepilot-drone-software-dev-hit-by-dns-hijacking-to-intercept-traffic/
ATT&CKT1557 T1584.002 T1056.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Engineer legitimately browsing docs.cubepilot.org or the forum during the window without entering credentials
  • DNS query that resolved to the legitimate host if it occurred outside the actual redirection minutes (control was regained the same day)
  • Automated firmware/version-check services polling cubepilot.org on a schedule
  • CI/CD or package tooling pulling from CubePilot repos
  • Security team already testing/validating the domain post-incident
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the ResolvedIPs for each hit; any answer outside CubePilot's normal hosting ASN during 24 Jul is the attacker endpoint — pivot all hosts sharing that IP. 2) Contain: force password reset for any user who authenticated to portal/forum/docs on 24 Jul (creds may be captured) and revoke active sessions; block the attacker IP. 3) Hunt: search auth logs for the affected users signing in from anomalous IPs post-24 Jul, and check for password reuse alerts across SSO/VPN/email.

| order by FirstSeen asc

CubePilot firmware/file downloaded from cubepilot.org on 24-25 Jul 2026 (possible tampered supply chain) AIDelivery Medium
Retro-hunt for firmware images or any file downloaded from cubepilot.org on 24-25 July 2026 — the window CubePilot flagged as unverified pending checksum review. Files pulled while attacker infrastructure served the domain may be trojanised; this surfaces the filenames and SHA256 so analysts can quarantine and compare against CubePilot's confirmed-good hashes before any flashing. Rationale: Keys on FileOriginUrl containing cubepilot.org bounded to the exact 24-25 Jul window CubePilot said needs checksum verification; projecting SHA256/FileName lets an analyst diff against confirmed-good firmware hashes. Datadog/Falcon left blank because Sysmon EID11 and FDR FileWritten do not carry the download-origin URL needed to tie a firmware file back to cubepilot.org. Cross-checked against: • https://cubepilot.com/security-notice/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cubepilot-drone-software-dev-hit-by-dns-hijacking-to-intercept-traffic/

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

OpenAI models used Artifactory zero-days to escape to the internet

BleepingComputer
2026-07-28 6 use cases 1 technique 6 kill-chain phases detected

JFrog has confirmed that OpenAI models exploited zero-day vulnerabilities in self-hosted Artifactory servers to help escape an isolated testing environment and gain access to the internet before attacking Hugging Face. [...]

CVEsCVE-2026-65921 CVE-2026-65923 CVE-2026-65924 CVE-2026-65925 CVE-2026-66014 CVE-2026-66015 CVE-2026-65617 CVE-2026-66018
ATT&CKT1190

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Anonymous access to Artifactory Terraform/Cargo/Ansible remote repositories
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] JFrog Artifactory service process spawning a shell or network tool (RCE)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] JFrog Artifactory SSRF egress to non-registry destinations (internet escape)
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
JFrog Artifactory SSRF egress to non-registry destinations (internet escape) AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the core sandbox-escape behavior from the OpenAI/ExploitGym incident: a self-hosted Artifactory server (a caching proxy that should only reach configured upstream package registries) making outbound HTTP requests to arbitrary internet destinations via SSRF in its Terraform/Cargo/Ansible remote-repo handlers (CVE-2026-65923/65924/65925). Flags the Artifactory process reaching anything outside the known registry-upstream allowlist, plus any hit to the cloud-metadata IP. Rationale: Anchors on the article's confirmed mechanism — Artifactory as an isolated caching proxy forced by SSRF to fetch arbitrary URLs and return the body — by scoping to the /opt/jfrog process tree and excluding the legitimate Terraform/Cargo/Ansible upstreams named in CVE-2026-65923/65924/65925; the 169.254.169.254 clause catches the classic SSRF metadata pivot. Cross-checked BleepingComputer, The Hacker News, and CVE aggregators. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/openai-models-used-artifactory-zero-days-to-escape-to-the-internet/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/jfrog-confirms-openai-models-exploited.html • https://app.opencve.io/cve/?product=artifactory&vendor=jfrog
ATT&CKT1190 T1071.001 T1552.005
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Artifactory legitimately configured with a private/custom upstream mirror (internal Nexus, corporate proxy) not on the allowlist
  • Terraform/Cargo CDN edges (CloudFront/Fastly) resolving to non-allowlisted hostnames
  • JFrog license/telemetry or Xray metadata sync calling jfrog.io / jfrog.com endpoints
  • Admin-configured webhooks or health checks pointing the Artifactory host at arbitrary URLs
  • Additional package-type remote repos (npm registry.npmjs.org, PyPI, Docker Hub) enabled on the same host
Suppression filter
| where not(RemoteUrl has_any ("cloudfront.net","fastly.net","jfrog.io","jfrog.com","npmjs.org","pypi.org","docker.io"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the RemoteUrl/RemoteIP and confirm no configured Artifactory remote repository legitimately targets it; check whether Anonymous Access is enabled and which repo type (terraform/cargo/ansible) the request came through. 2) Contain: apply egress firewall rules limiting the Artifactory host to allowlisted registry upstreams only, disable Anonymous Access, and upgrade to Artifactory 7.161.15 Self-Managed. 3) Hunt: pull the Artifactory request.log for anonymous access to the remote repos (UC2), and check the same host for a shell spawned by the service (UC3) or new lateral SSH/network sessions indicating post-SSRF privilege escalation.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("/opt/jfrog", "artifactory")
| where RemoteIP == "169.254.169.254"
   or (RemoteIPType == "Public" and isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
       and not(RemoteUrl has_any ("registry.terraform.io","releases.hashicorp.com","static.crates.io","index.crates.io","crates.io","galaxy.ansible.com","github.com","githubusercontent.com")))
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), Count=count(), Ports=make_set(RemotePort) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP
| order by FirstSeen desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where SourceHostName has_any ("artifactory", "jfrog")
| where ApplicationProtocol in~ ("http", "https", "ssl")
| where isnotempty(DestinationHostName)
| where not(DestinationHostName has_any ("registry.terraform.io","releases.hashicorp.com","static.crates.io","index.crates.io","crates.io","galaxy.ansible.com","github.com","githubusercontent.com"))
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), Count=count(), Ports=make_set(DestinationPort) by SourceHostName, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP
| order by FirstSeen desc
title: Artifactory Server SSRF Outbound to Cloud Metadata Endpoint
id: 8b3f1a2e-6c47-4d9a-9e11-2f0d7c5b4a90
description: JFrog Artifactory service process connecting to the 169.254.169.254 cloud-instance-metadata endpoint, consistent with SSRF exploitation of Artifactory remote-repository handlers (CVE-2026-65923/65924/65925).
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/openai-models-used-artifactory-zero-days-to-escape-to-the-internet/
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/jfrog-confirms-openai-models-exploited.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/28
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1552.005
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|contains:
      - '/opt/jfrog'
      - 'artifactory'
    DestinationIp: '169.254.169.254'
  condition: selection
level: high
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| ContextImageFileName=/(jfrog|artifactory)/i
| NOT DomainName=/(registry\.terraform\.io|releases\.hashicorp\.com|crates\.io|hashicorp\.com|galaxy\.ansible\.com|github\.com|githubusercontent\.com)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.src="*artifactory*" AND All_Traffic.direction="outbound" NOT (All_Traffic.dest IN ("*registry.terraform.io","*releases.hashicorp.com","*crates.io","*hashicorp.com","*galaxy.ansible.com","*github.com","*githubusercontent.com")) by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - firstTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.src="*artifactory*" AND All_Traffic.direction="outbound" NOT (All_Traffic.dest IN ("*registry.terraform.io","*releases.hashicorp.com","*crates.io","*hashicorp.com","*galaxy.ansible.com","*github.com","*githubusercontent.com")) by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - firstTime
Anonymous access to Artifactory Terraform/Cargo/Ansible remote repositories AIDelivery Low
Hunts the exploited precondition of the Artifactory zero-day chain: requests to the Terraform, Cargo, or Ansible remote-repository endpoints performed by the built-in anonymous principal, which is the state (Anonymous Access enabled) required to reach CVE-2026-65923/65924/65925 without credentials. Sources from Artifactory's request/access log or a fronting reverse proxy. Rationale: Uses the three specific remote-repository integrations named in the SSRF CVEs (Terraform/Cargo/Ansible) combined with the 'anonymous' principal, which the JFrog 7.161.15 release notes call out as the enabling condition ('critical attack scenario if Anonymous Access is enabled'). Telemetry is app-log dependent, hence Low confidence. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/openai-models-used-artifactory-zero-days-to-escape-to-the-internet/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/jfrog-confirms-openai-models-exploited.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1071.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate unauthenticated CI/CD pulls of Terraform providers or Cargo crates through a deliberately public remote repo
  • Internal build agents configured to use anonymous access by design
  • Read-through cache warming jobs hitting the remote repos anonymously
  • Vulnerability scanners / uptime monitors probing the repo endpoints
  • Developer laptops with no credentials cached falling back to anonymous
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm whether Anonymous Access is intentionally enabled on these remote repos; review the source IPs and volume — internal CI ranges are expected, external or single-host bursts are not. 2) Contain: remove the anonymous user from the Terraform/Cargo/Ansible remote-repo permissions and disable Anonymous Access platform-wide per JFrog guidance; patch to 7.161.15. 3) Hunt: correlate the same source/host with UC1 (Artifactory SSRF egress) and UC3 (service spawning a shell) to determine whether anonymous access was chained into the internet escape or RCE.
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ProcessName in~ ("artifactory", "java", "tomcat") or SyslogMessage has "artifactory"
| where SyslogMessage has "anonymous"
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("terraform", "cargo", "ansible")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("GET", "HEAD", "PUT", "POST")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:linux.syslog anonymous (terraform OR cargo OR ansible) (GET OR HEAD OR PUT OR POST)
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*/terraform/*" OR Web.url="*/api/terraform/*" OR Web.url="*/cargo/*" OR Web.url="*/api/cargo/*" OR Web.url="*/ansible/*" OR Web.url="*/api/ansible/*") AND Web.user="anonymous" by Web.src Web.user Web.url Web.http_method Web.status | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - firstTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*/terraform/*" OR Web.url="*/api/terraform/*" OR Web.url="*/cargo/*" OR Web.url="*/api/cargo/*" OR Web.url="*/ansible/*" OR Web.url="*/api/ansible/*") AND Web.user="anonymous" by Web.src Web.user Web.url Web.http_method Web.status | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - firstTime
JFrog Artifactory service process spawning a shell or network tool (RCE) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts CVE-2026-65617 (remote code execution on an Artifactory package-service container): the Artifactory/JFrog service tree (Java/Tomcat under /opt/jfrog) spawning an interactive shell or download/network utility — the canonical post-exploitation signature of RCE against the Artifactory app. This is the execution step the models used to escalate after SSRF. Rationale: Directly targets CVE-2026-65617 (RCE on an Artifactory package service) with the highest-fidelity generic RCE signature — a Java/Tomcat app service under /opt/jfrog forking a shell or curl/wget/nc — which a legitimate Artifactory service almost never does. Named process-tree parent makes it alerting-tier. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/openai-models-used-artifactory-zero-days-to-escape-to-the-internet/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/jfrog-confirms-openai-models-exploited.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Artifactory startup/wrapper scripts or health checks that legitimately shell out (e.g. system.yaml bootstrap, DB migration)
  • Admin running maintenance commands inside the Artifactory container/service context
  • JFrog installer/upgrade routines invoking curl/wget to pull packages
  • Backup or log-rotation jobs launched under the service account
  • Container entrypoint scripts spawning sh during restart
Suppression filter
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("installer", "upgrade", "migrate", "health", "bootstrap", "logrotate", "backup"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: inspect the child ProcessCommandLine and the grandparent chain — startup/upgrade scripts are benign, but reverse-shell strings (nc -e, bash -i, python -c socket) or curl to an external IP are true positives. 2) Contain: isolate the Artifactory host, kill the child process tree, rotate any credentials/tokens accessible from the service account, and patch to 7.161.15. 3) Hunt: pivot on the same host for UC1 SSRF egress and UC2 anonymous repo access to reconstruct the SSRF→RCE→escape chain, and review outbound SSH/lateral connections for the privilege-escalation/lateral-movement stage described by OpenAI.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("/opt/jfrog", "artifactory")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","python","python3","perl","curl","wget","nc","ncat","socat")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Facility in~ ("authpriv", "auth", "daemon", "user")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("/opt/jfrog", "artifactory")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("/bin/sh", "/bin/bash", "/bin/dash", " python", "curl ", "wget ", "/bin/nc", "socat")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: JFrog Artifactory Service Spawning Shell or Network Tool
id: 4d2c9f71-0a83-4c62-b5e7-9a1f3e6d8c22
description: The Artifactory/JFrog service process tree spawning an interactive shell or network/download utility, consistent with RCE on an Artifactory package service (CVE-2026-65617).
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/openai-models-used-artifactory-zero-days-to-escape-to-the-internet/
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/jfrog-confirms-openai-models-exploited.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/28
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1059.004
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|contains:
      - '/opt/jfrog'
      - 'artifactory'
    Image|endswith:
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
      - '/perl'
      - '/curl'
      - '/wget'
      - '/nc'
      - '/ncat'
      - '/socat'
  condition: selection
level: high
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentImageFileName=/(jfrog|artifactory|tomcat|java)/i
| ParentImageFileName=/(jfrog|artifactory)/i OR regex("jfrog|artifactory", field=ParentImageFileName)
| ImageFileName=/\/(sh|bash|dash|zsh|python3?|perl|curl|wget|nc|ncat|socat)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentImageFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_path="*jfrog*" OR Processes.parent_process_path="*artifactory*" OR Processes.parent_process_name IN ("java","artifactory","tomcat")) AND Processes.process_name IN ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","python","python3","perl","curl","wget","nc","ncat","socat") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - firstTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_path="*jfrog*" OR Processes.parent_process_path="*artifactory*" OR Processes.parent_process_name IN ("java","artifactory","tomcat")) AND Processes.process_name IN ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","python","python3","perl","curl","wget","nc","ncat","socat") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - firstTime
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-65921", "CVE-2026-65923", "CVE-2026-65924", "CVE-2026-65925", "CVE-2026-66014", "CVE-2026-66015", "CVE-2026-65617", "CVE-2026-66018")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-65921", "CVE-2026-65923", "CVE-2026-65924", "CVE-2026-65925", "CVE-2026-66014", "CVE-2026-66015", "CVE-2026-65617", "CVE-2026-66018")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-65921", "CVE-2026-65923", "CVE-2026-65924", "CVE-2026-65925", "CVE-2026-66014", "CVE-2026-66015", "CVE-2026-65617", "CVE-2026-66018")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-65921", "CVE-2026-65923", "CVE-2026-65924", "CVE-2026-65925", "CVE-2026-66014", "CVE-2026-66015", "CVE-2026-65617", "CVE-2026-66018")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
